name: Heroic
tagline: Spotify's time-series database on Bigtable or Cassandra plus Elasticsearch; deprecated in 2021.
description: Heroic is the time-series database Spotify built for its internal monitoring. It stores metric samples in Google Cloud Bigtable or Apache Cassandra and keeps series metadata and tags in Elasticsearch, which powers tag-based lookups and suggestions; a Java service on top offers an HTTP API, its own query language with aggregations, and federation that fans queries out across clusters in several regions. Spotify open-sourced it in 2015 and published a deprecation notice in March 2021 with the final 2.3.18 release, saying it would no longer improve or release Heroic; the repository is archived. It remains a readable example of separating metric storage from metadata indexing, but new deployments should use Prometheus-compatible systems.
statusNote: Spotify deprecated Heroic in March 2021 (final release 2.3.18) and archived the repository. Use Mimir, VictoriaMetrics or M3.
basedOn: Google Cloud Bigtable or Apache Cassandra, with Elasticsearch

scale.notes: Storage scales with the Bigtable or Cassandra backend; federation fans queries out to independent regional clusters.

strengths: Separates sample storage (Bigtable/Cassandra) from tag indexing (Elasticsearch)
weaknesses: Deprecated and archived; no security fixes
Requires running Bigtable or Cassandra plus Elasticsearch
Not compatible with PromQL or the Prometheus ecosystem
useCases: Maintaining existing Heroic deployments during migration
notIdealFor: Small teams without Cassandra or Elasticsearch expertise
